clusters.name: Statistics
clusters.fact: Statistics summarizes data using measures like mean, median, and range.

range.text: The difference between the highest and lowest values in a data set.

mode.text: The value that appears most often in a data set.

clusters.name: Probability
clusters.fact: Probability measures how likely an event is, from impossible to certain.

outcome.text: A single possible result of an experiment or trial.

event.text: A set of one or more outcomes — "rolling an even number" is an event made up of three individual outcomes.

sample space.text: The full set of every possible outcome of an experiment or event.

clusters.name: Graphs & charts
clusters.fact: Graphs and charts turn raw numbers into a picture that's easier to read at a glance.

line graph.text: A chart connecting data points with a line, typically used to show change over time.

bridges.fact: Sample bridges the two: statistics describes a sample, and probability predicts how well it represents the whole population.

info.text: A subset drawn from a larger population, used to make inferences about the whole.

bridges.fact: Distribution bridges the two: it's a probability idea that's almost always shown as a graph, like a histogram's shape.

info.text: A description of how likely each possible outcome is.
